title: Naming thread pool threads
context: How do you name the threads in a pool, and why does it matter?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Pass a ThreadFactory to the executor. Build it with a name prefix and a counter, for example `order-worker-%d` using `ThreadFactoryBuilder` from Guava, or a small lambda that sets `thread.setName`. Good names show up in thread dumps, logs and metrics, so you can see which pool is busy or stuck. Without a factory, threads are named pool-1-thread-1, which tells you nothing about the code.

points.title: Use a ThreadFactory
points.why: The factory sets each thread's name when it is created.

points.title: Debugging
points.why: Named threads make thread dumps and logs point at the right pool.
